free_tier.stated: Hourly GPU rental with a published low-price tier, quoted from the vendor's student page: RTX 3080 at CNY 0.77 an hour, RTX 3090 at CNY 1.10, RTX 4090 24GB at CNY 1.65, RTX 4090 48GB at CNY 2.53. The same four prices appear on the individual-developer page, which means the student page is a label rather than a separate discount. The vendor also states elastic cloud hosts from CNY 0.65 an hour on the business page.

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
chaining: CNY 1.65 an hour is the middle of the Chinese 4090 market and the 48 GB card at CNY 2.53 is the cheap route past the 24 GB limit, which is what decides whether a 32B model fits.
limits_note: Nothing throttles a job; the constraint is the hourly meter plus availability, since the cheapest tier is a shared pool and the vendor's own business page prices the same cards higher for dedicated use.

evidence.proved: the page's price cards, captured by the search index because the page extractor returned only navigation text: RTX 3080 ¥0.77/小时, RTX 3090 ¥1.10/小时, RTX 4090 24G ¥1.65/小时, RTX 4090 48G ¥2.53/小时, quoted
the individual-developer page carries the same four prices, which shows the student label does not change the rate
an independent aggregator lists 智星云 4090 at USD 0.192 per card-hour on an annual rate for CN-华东 with eight cards per instance, a different billing mode from the hourly student price

notes: New to the corpus. The page HTML renders its price cards in script and the extractor returned 274 words of navigation on both /stu and /user, so the numbers come from the search index's rendering of those exact URLs and are recorded as reported rather than documented. Two independent renderings of the same page agree, and the aggregator's annual-rate figure is consistent with a lower rate for a longer commitment.
